newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's secularist media hails government vote win.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's secularist media hails government vote win.

text.p: Turkey's secularist media on Sunday applauded the success of the new anti-Islamist government in a confidence vote which it won by a clear margin after months of political chaos.
"Congratulations. Parliament produced a 'democratic solution'," a headline in the liberal Yeni Yuzyil daily said.
"A new age. The Islamist-led government, which strained Turkey for a year, is consigned to history," said the mass circulation Sabah newspaper.
Parliament voted 281 to 256 on Saturday to approve a coalition under conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz that is designed to keep the big Islam-based Welfare Party out of power.
Yilmaz and cabinet ministers in his left-right alliance were to visit the mausoleum of Turkey's secularist founder Mustafa Kemal Ataturk on Sunday in a traditional show of respect.

The new government has vowed to reassert Turkey's bid for greater integration with Europe after a year in which Islamist former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan sought to strengthen the secular, Moslem nation's links with the Islamic world.
Yilmaz has also promised to restrict Islamic education -- one of the most sensitive issues in the battle for the country's hearts and minds.
The new prime minister was conciliatory after the vote.
"We know Turkey has very serious problems but there is no issue our country cannot solve with tolerance, compromise and the power you have given us," he told parliament.
The last months of predecessor Erbakan's tenure were marred by fierce public debate over Islam, democracy and the right of the influential army to play politics.
